layer.description: Next.js 15 fullstack app with TypeScript, Tailwind, Prisma, and Vitest

resources.name: project-context
resources.content:
# Next.js Fullstack App

## Tech Stack
- Next.js 15 (App Router)
- TypeScript 5.x (strict mode)
- Tailwind CSS 4
- Prisma ORM with PostgreSQL
- Vitest for testing
- pnpm as package manager

## Commands
- `pnpm dev` — Start dev server
- `pnpm build` — Production build
- `pnpm test` — Run tests with Vitest
- `pnpm lint` — ESLint + Prettier check
- `pnpm db:migrate` — Run Prisma migrations
- `pnpm db:seed` — Seed development data

## Architecture
- `src/app/` — Next.js App Router pages and layouts
- `src/components/ui/` — Shared UI primitives (shadcn/ui)
- `src/components/features/` — Feature-specific components
- `src/lib/` — Utilities, types, and shared logic
- `src/server/` — Server-only code (API routes, DB queries)

## Conventions
- Use named exports, not default exports
- Components use PascalCase filenames
- Utilities use camelCase filenames
- All database queries go through `src/server/db/`
- Use `cn()` from `@/lib/utils` for conditional classNames
- Prefer server components; add `use client` only when needed

## Rules
- NEVER modify migration files after they've been committed
- Always use server actions instead of API routes for mutations
- Do not add new dependencies without asking first
- Keep components under 200 lines
- All user-facing strings must use the i18n system

resources.name: react-components
resources.content:
# React Component Standards

- Use functional components with explicit TypeScript props interface
- Destructure props in the function signature
- Use CSS Modules or Tailwind utility classes, never inline styles
- Include aria-labels for interactive elements
- Keep components under 150 lines — split into sub-components
- Prefer composition over prop drilling
- Co-locate tests: `Component.test.tsx` next to `Component.tsx`

resources.name: api-routes
resources.content:
# API Route Standards

- Validate all inputs with Zod schemas
- Return consistent response shape: `{ success, data?, error? }`
- Include rate limiting on write endpoints
- Log all errors with structured context (requestId, userId, endpoint)
- Never expose internal error details to clients
- Use proper HTTP status codes

resources.name: database
resources.content:
# Database Rules

- All schema changes go through Prisma migrations
- Use transactions for multi-table writes
- Add indexes for columns used in WHERE clauses and JOINs
- Implement soft deletes (deletedAt column) for user-facing data
- Table names: plural snake_case
- Column names: snake_case
